gloss: to become skilled; to get used to

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {手慣|てな}れていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to become skilled at; to become practiced; to get the hang of
definitions.explanation: To become proficient at something through repeated experience, so that one can do it smoothly and without difficulty.

examples.japanese: {手慣|てな}れた⟦{手|て}つき→手つき：30134_tetsuki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
さすが⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手慣|てな}れたもので、⟦{作業|さぎょう}→作業：02775_sagyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{速|はや}い→速い：00514_hayai⟧。
examples.english: As expected from someone experienced, the work is fast.

examples.japanese: ⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す→繰り返す：02051_kurikaesu⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{手慣|てな}れてきて、⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦しなく→する：00392_suru⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: After repeating it many times, I got the hang of it and stopped making mistakes.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ (hand) and ⟦{慣|な}れる→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧ (to get used to). Describes the kind of proficiency that comes from hands-on practice. Most commonly encountered in the past-tense form {手慣|てな}れた as a modifier.

USAGE:
Almost always appears as {手慣|てな}れた + noun (practiced, skilled) to describe someone performing a task with smooth, experienced ease. The phrase {手慣|てな}れた⟦{手|て}つき→手つき：30134_tetsuki⟧ (practiced hand movements) is especially common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手慣|てな}れた⟦{手|て}つき→手つき：30134_tetsuki⟧ — with practiced hands, with skilled movements
- {手慣|てな}れた⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧ — in a practiced manner
- {手慣|てな}れたもの — something one is well-practiced at

FORMS:
Ichidan (る) verb. Intransitive.
- {手慣|てな}れる → {手慣|てな}れた → {手慣|てな}れて

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{慣|な}れる→慣れる：00870_nareru⟧ — to get used to; the base verb, broader in meaning
- ⟦{熟練|じゅくれん}→熟練：09081_jukuren⟧ — mastery, skilled expertise; more formal
- ⟦{手際|てぎわ}→手際：06657_tegiwa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ — to be efficient, deft; focuses on the quality of execution
